interest: This file provides a compelling window into the severe social crises and public sentiment in occupied Japan in early 1947, as monitored and analyzed by SCAP's Civil Information and Education Section. It is particularly valuable for revealing contemporary justifications for the black market (open-air markets), which magazine commentators and operators defended not as mere criminal opportunism but as an indispensable, moral lifeline for destitute repatriates, war widows, and unemployed veterans. Furthermore, the report offers poignant documentation of the plight of an estimated 4,755 war orphans, the realities of reform institutions and orphanages (both municipal and Catholic), and the tragic neglect experienced by disabled veterans at Sagamigahara National Hospital amid inflation and acute shortages.
overview: This file consists of an October 1947 transmittal despatch from the United States Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo to the Department of State, an internal State Department routing note, and an enclosed GHQ/SCAP Civil Information and Education (CI&E) Section Publications Analysis (No. 91, dated January 24, 1947) entitled 'Welfare.' The report analyzes contemporary Japanese magazine articles regarding acute postwar domestic social problems. Major subjects include the crisis of war orphans and abandoned infants, rising juvenile delinquency, the inadequate institutional care and public indifference facing demobilized and disabled soldiers (highlighted by conditions at Sagamigahara National Hospital), the provisions of the new Law of Protection of Livelihood, and widespread journalistic defenses of open-air black markets as essential survival mechanisms for impoverished citizens.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of five copies of a SCAP Civil Information and Education Section report on Japanese welfare problems dated January 24, 1947.
subfiles.from: Counselor of Mission, United States Political Adviser for Japan (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1317 from the Counselor of Mission at the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo transmits five copies of a GHQ/SCAP Civil Information and Education Section report entitled 'Welfare' (dated January 24, 1947) to the Department of State. Drafted by Richard H. Bushner, the despatch was received in Washington on October 17, 1947, and filed on November 20, 1947. It forwards intelligence on Japanese social issues and press discussions under the Allied Occupation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1317 Transmitting SCAP Report on Welfare Problems in Japan

subfiles.about: Internal State Department comment highlighting that the January 1947 report reflects Japanese magazine preoccupation with repatriation, neglected veterans, and defenses of the black market.
subfiles.summary: An internal State Department note initialed MGJ highlights the January 24, 1947 date of the enclosed SCAP report. The author observes that during that period, Japanese magazine articles on welfare were heavily preoccupied with repatriation and the public's indifference toward wounded and unemployed ex-servicemen. The note also emphasizes that several surveyed articles explicitly defended the moral basis of black market operations.
subfiles.title: State Department Routing Note on SCAP Welfare Report

subfiles.about: Analysis of Japanese magazine commentary on post-war social welfare issues, including war orphans, juvenile delinquency, repatriates, disabled veterans, and the black market.
subfiles.from: Civil Information & Education Section, Analysis and Research Division, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ, SCAP)
subfiles.summary: This SCAP CI&E Publications Analysis report surveys contemporary Japanese magazine articles examining severe post-war welfare challenges in late 1946 and early 1947. It examines the crisis of homeless children and war orphans, assessing conditions in asylums and reform facilities such as the Itabashi home, Saredio School, and the Seto Boys' Home. The report also addresses the difficult reintegration of repatriates and demobilized soldiers, detailing acute hardships and inadequate prosthetic supplies for amputees at Sagamigahara National Hospital. Finally, it explores extensive magazine commentary defending open-air black markets as morally justified and necessary means of survival for destitute veterans and citizens amid rampant shortages.
subfiles.title: SCAP CI&E Publications Analysis No. 91: 'Welfare'
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
